A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GradSkip research work. Their main text, figures, algorithms, equations and appendices are readable, allowing additions, removals and relocated material to be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 Section 5 reports original logistic-regression experiments on synthetic and Australian data, including convergence, gradient computations and simulated total-time results.

after.justification: v2 Section 5 and Figures 1–3 report original convergence and gradient-computation results on synthetic and Australian data.

M1.justification: v1 leaves stochastic gradients to future work. v2 introduces VR-GradSkip+ in Algorithm 3, replacing full gradients in the shift and iterate updates with unbiased stochastic estimators, including variance-reduced estimators. The existing GradSkip and GradSkip+ procedures remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both retain regularized binary logistic regression on synthetic and Australian data. Coverage narrows through removal of v1 Section 5.2's equal, random and condition-dependent device-speed scenarios. The new Australian gradient-count comparison uses an existing dataset and task.

E2.justification: ProxSkip remains the sole experimentally evaluated baseline against GradSkip. Newly discussing ProxSkip-VR and accelerated gradient descent does not introduce additional empirical comparators.

E3.justification: After aligning smoothness constants with condition numbers, Figure 1's intermediate maximum condition number changes from 10^5 to two settings, 10^4 and 10^6. The Australian comparison replaces timing plots spanning 2,000 communication rounds with gradient-count plots spanning 3,000 rounds and explicitly specifies an equal partition across 20 clients.

E4.justification: v1 Section 5.2 and Figure 3 test when heterogeneous device speeds produce runtime savings; this entire sensitivity analysis disappears from v2, including its equal-speed control. The conditioning sweep in Figure 1 is revised, while Figure 2's client-count sensitivity analysis is retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The stochastic variance assumptions added in v2 are theoretical assumptions, not empirical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Figure 1 replaces the intermediate gradient-count ratio 15.24 at maximum condition number 10^5 with 10.23 at 10^4 and 18.17 at 10^6; endpoint ratios 2.576 and 19.78 remain. Figure 2 retains ratios 3.994, 15.88 and 61.89. v1 Figure 3's total-time ratios 1.0, 2.105 and 2.720 disappear, while v2 Figure 3 adds an Australian gradient-count ratio of 2.176. These are replaced settings and different metrics, not same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: v2 adds stochastic-estimator Assumption B.1, an augmented Lyapunov function, Theorem B.2 and supporting proofs. It replaces v1 Appendix C.2's direct GradSkip+ proof with a specialization argument in Appendix D.2 and removes the waiting-time bounds from v1 Section 5.2. As printed, Theorem B.2's B=0 branch sets beta to zero for Lemma D.1's parameters, leaving the claimed linear-rate specialization inconsistent.

C1.justification: v2 Section 2.3 introduces stochastic variance-reduced gradient skipping as a third main contribution, whereas v1 identifies stochastic gradients only as future work. The central claims of accelerated communication and reduced local gradient computation are retained.

C2.justification: v2 explains computational savings through the number k of ill-conditioned clients, replacing the n-limit discussion with an n/k interpretation and applying k=8 to Australian data. It removes the full-batch-only limitation and waiting-time interpretation, and adds a rationale for studying local training despite accelerated gradient descent's matching communication complexity.

D1.justification: v2 explicitly documents the equal 20-client Australian partition and clarifies that the synthetic regularization parameter equals mu and that theoretical hyperparameters include stepsizes and probabilities. v1's device-time assignments and unit communication-time assumption disappear with the timing experiment. The Python/RAY implementation information is retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds references concerning stochastic estimators, client sampling and local representation learning, including Gorbunov et al. (2020b), Grudzien et al. (2023) and Collins et al. (2022). Remark 3.7 discusses positioning against accelerated gradient descent, and Appendix B positions VR-GradSkip+ as combining ProxSkip-VR with gradient skipping.

P1.justification: The abstract is rewritten and existing prose receives terminology and grammar edits. GradSkip+ special cases move from main-text Section 4.2 to Appendix D.3, and contribution and experiment sections are adjusted. Most existing method exposition remains closely matched.

P2.justification: v2 changes the main text and references from two columns to one and reformats equations and algorithm blocks. Figure 1 expands from three to four rows; plots introduce condition-number axes, threshold markers and color distinctions. The nine-panel timing Figure 3 is replaced by four gradient-analysis panels, and Algorithm 3 is added.

improvement.justification: v2 develops the stochastic extension left as future work in v1 and adds Australian computational-savings evidence. However, it removes the timing study supporting the system-heterogeneity motivation. It also replaces the direct GradSkip+ proof with a specialization of Theorem B.2 whose stated parameters give beta=0 and an undefined error-floor term, failing to recover the claimed linear rate as printed. The useful additions, lost empirical support and unresolved proof inconsistency prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
